title: fix(service-storage)!: stored bytes outside the inline allow-list are served as attachments, with nosniff and a sandbox CSP
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户在附件、文件下载里打开文件时:图片、PDF、纯文本、音视频照旧在新标签页里直接预览;其余类型(含 SVG、HTML)改为下载到本地,不再在浏览器里直接打开。
- 文件存储加固:统一一条规则决定哪些类型可以在浏览器里直接显示,本地存储与 S3 签名链接一致执行。
- 若有人依赖在浏览器里直接打开 SVG 或网页类附件,现在会变成下载;页面里用图片标签显示的 SVG 不受影响,可整体撤回本改动。
- 无

## What changes

One rule for answering stored bytes, stated once in `packages/services/service-storage/src/served-bytes-policy.ts` and applied by every door that answers them:

1. **Inline only for the allow-list.** `INLINE_CONTENT_TYPES`: raster images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP), PDF, plain text, and common audio and video types. Every other type, SVG and HTML included, and a missing or malformed type, is answered as an `attachment`. The type is judged by its essence (case and parameters dropped), and a caller asking for `inline` never overrides the list.
2. **`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every answer.**
3. **A sandbox `Content-Security-Policy` on every answer** (inline or not): `sandbox; default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`.

Doors held to it (census of every route that answers stored bytes):

| Door | Origin | What it now does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/storage/_local/raw/:token` (local adapter) | the app's own | sets all four headers from the rule: type (essence), disposition, `nosniff`, CSP |
| S3 adapter `getPresignedDownload` (also behind `getSignedUrl`, and so behind `GET /files/:fileId`, `GET /files/:fileId/url` and the record-file read) | the bucket's | always bakes `ResponseContentType` (essence) and `ResponseContentDisposition` (rule 1). A signed `GetObject` URL can carry no other response header, so rules 2 and 3 are the bucket's to send |

`GET /files/:fileId` and `GET /files/:fileId/url` serve no bytes of their own: both mint through `mintDownloadUrl`, which lands on one of the two rows above. No other route in the repository answers stored bytes (searched: `storage.download(` callers, `content-type` / `content-disposition` writers across `packages/**`). `content-disposition.ts` is now reached only through the rule. The docs page `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` gains a short "How a downloaded file is answered" section.

Not in this PR: restricting the declared type at upload time to what the bytes are. It is reported to the seat as a decision (it needs a storage-contract choice for uploads that go straight to S3).

## Tests

- `packages/services/service-storage/src/served-bytes-policy.test.ts` (14): the allow-list table, essence parsing, the local raw route's headers through `registerStorageRoutes`, and the S3 signed URL's baked parameters.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/stored-bytes-served-disposition.dogfood.test.ts` (6): a real boot with the local adapter: presign, byte PUT, commit, the download door's signed link, and the raw route's answer, through the real Hono app.
- Controls in both files: an ordinary PNG (and PDF) still previews inline under its own type and bytes; green before and after.

## Acceptance notes

- The served type for an allow-listed `text/plain` keeps a `charset` parameter when one was declared; every other type is answered by its essence alone.
- `PresignedDownloadOptions.disposition`'s TSDoc in `packages/spec/src/contracts/storage-service.ts` still reads "`inline` previews in the browser (default)". It stays true for allow-listed types; it is left untouched here to keep `packages/spec` out of this diff.
- An image element (`img`) showing a stored SVG keeps rendering it (measured in Chromium): an image element ignores the disposition.
